Comparison

First-screen jobInput reachableProof visible without pressing playSectionsRisk
A nowShows the product as a stillbelow the cropYes, but far down5Video is the 3rd thing; the crop and the video say the same thing twice
BThe video is the pitchbelow a 16:9 videoOnly in the poster3If nobody presses play, the page is a picture and a form
CPitch + action togetherin the first screenOnly in the poster3Video is smaller (≈520 px); stacks into B's order on narrow screens
DB + a fallback for non-playerssame as BYes, small4A little repetition with the video
EChoice of mediumsame as BOne click away3Tabs need a click to see the non-video media; most people won't

My recommendation: B — your order, with the video kept to ≤ 760 px — and drop "Bob doesn't just read it. He runs it."

  • The video already is that section. Its poster is the frame where the before/after appears with "the bug reproduced at the old commit and is gone at the new one", so the claim is visible without pressing play. Keeping the band says the same thing a third time, and far down the page.
  • The real-step crop goes too. It is what the video shows in motion; it was there before the video existed, and it pushed everything else down.
  • B, not full-width. At 860 px the input sits at the fold; at 760 px it is comfortably in the first screen on a 1440×900 laptop, and the page stays three blocks: pitch, action, library.
  • Alternative: C (title + input left, video right) if the input must be visible on a 1366×768 laptop — the price is a smaller video (~520 px), and this video has small UI text, so people would go full-screen anyway.
  • Safety net, optional: D's strip (two thumbnails and a line) for visitors who never press play.
